column1: # The RFC 7529 RSCALE divergence corpus: one case per way ical-rs and libical
# 3.0.20 with ICU 76 answer differently, with ical-rs's answer and the reason.
# Four tab-separated fields: the DTSTART, the RRULE, the occurrences ical-rs
# yields, and why. The run of 2026-10-29 split on 458 of 2,370 cases, every one
# Hand-curated. Never edit an expected value to make a case pass.

column4: RFC 7529 4.2: 5L is a leap month following the 5th, which this calendar never has, so SKIP decides and OMIT drops it; libical drops the L and reads the 5th month. 233 cases.
The same, SKIP=FORWARD moving the missing leap month to the 6th month (RFC 7529 4.1); libical reads the 5th.

INTERVAL counts periods from the one DTSTART falls in (RFC 5545 3.3.10); libical starts its non-Gregorian walk elsewhere, skipping DTSTART and every other year it implies. 130 cases, every scale but the Gregorian.
The same lattice split at a monthly frequency.
ICU4X dates Chinese New Year 2027 on 6 February, from the Hong Kong Observatory tables, as published calendars do; ICU4C computes 7 February astronomically. 12 cases.
Hebrew year 5806: ICU4X and python convertdate 2.4.1 put 8 Adar I on 2046-02-14, ICU4C 76 a day later, so every date of that year lands a day late in libical. 4 cases.

Past 2100 both libraries approximate the Chinese calendar, ICU4X by mean lunations and ICU4C astronomically, and they place leap months differently (a 5L in 2104 for ICU4C only). Neither is known right; ical-rs answers what ICU4X computes. 14 cases, Chinese and Dangi.

RFC 7529 4.1: SKIP=FORWARD moves a missing leap month to the month after it, the 6th. In a year with an earlier leap month (2020, with 4L) libical counts by ordinal and lands on the 5th. 42 cases with the 6L ones, Chinese and Dangi.
No Hebrew year has a 6L, the leap month being 5L, so SKIP=FORWARD moves it to the month after the 6th, Nisan; libical reads Adar, the 6th itself. 7 cases.
A Chinese year of 354 days has no 355th day, so it yields nothing that year; libical spills into the first day of the next year. 6 cases.
JAPANESE counts as the Gregorian calendar, its eras naming years a rule never reads; libical jumps from 2018 to 2049 at the 2019 era change. 4 cases.
SKIP=FORWARD moves a missing 30th to the first of the next month (RFC 7529 4.1), 1 Tishrei across the year included; libical drops that one and repeats another. 6 cases.
